To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the profile of a γ-ray giant flare of Sgr 1806-20, a magnetar, was measured for the first 0.6 seconds of the event with an energy resolution of about one part per thousand.

the giant flare of the magnetar SGR 1806–20 had a peak of 107 photons cm-2 s-1, reached 50 ms after the flare onset, then gradually decreased with superposed oscillations possibly representing repeated energy releases at 60 ms intervals, with an inferred total energy of 1047 erg.

we have determined the profile of the giant soft γ-ray repeaters flare of SGR 1806–20 with a time resolution better than 5 ms, and that the flare is composed of repeated energy injections separated by 60 ms.

the study of a giant flare from the soft γ ray repeater SGR 1806-20, a possible Magnetar.
the study of magnetars and the physical mechanism of the giant flares.

the giant flare was a series of energy injections from an extremely strong magnetic field, and the energy injection mechanism was very efficient.
